item.title: CXMT's innovative 4F² DRAM marks breakthrough in China's push into server memory chips: experts
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11 14:25:00
CXMT Photo: VCG China's leading memory chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) plans to launch a new-generation DDR5 RDIMM server-geared memory chip that leverages 4F² dynamic random access memory (DRAM) architecture by the end of 2026, company President Cao Kanyu said at an industry conference on Saturday. The move signals that Chinese suppliers are beginning to challenge more demanding system-level applications, quickening the pace from product iteration to architecture-level innovation, according to Chinese industry experts. The move marks China's latest push into architecture-level DRAM innovation and server-class memory validation, two areas long dominated by Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix and Micron Technology, Tian Feng, president of the Fast Think Institute and former dean of the Intelligence Industry Research Institute at SenseTime, told the Global Times on Sunday. Cao said that his company intends to use the 4F² architecture to overcome the engineering barriers in the server memory market. According to the company, at the core of CXMT's new platform is the Vertical Surrounded Gate transistor, which addresses current leakage and short-channel effects while increasing storage density. The design allows for higher storage density by moving from the industry's mainstream 6F² layout toward more compact 4F² architecture. By changing the structure to 4F², DRAM manufacturers can increase the cell density of each chip by 30 - 50 percent. CXMT has published more than 300 patents related to the 4F² architecture, which underscores the company's deepening intellectual property efforts to develop next-generation memory technologies, according to Cao. The planned launch of the new chip is an attempt by CXMT to expand into the server memory market. In the server memory segment, a few foreign chipmakers have held the upper hand, while CXMT's business had focused on consumer electronics, according to Shanghai-based Yicai.com. Experts said that the commercialization of the 4F² architecture is significant for the broader DRAM sector. "While the world's top three memory makers are advancing their own 4F² or similar 3D DRAM roadmaps, none has achieved large-scale commercialization yet," Tian said. If CXMT becomes one of the first vendors to bring 4F²-based products to market, it would not only gain an early position in the next-generation memory race, but also strengthen China's foothold in the high-end semiconductor supply chain, he noted. If the new architecture can be implemented stably this time, its manufacturing capabilities and reliability would demonstrate that it has met server-grade standards -- eligible for entry into the high-end chip market, Ma Jihua, a veteran industry analyst told the Global Times on Sunday. It aligns with the development path Chinese DRAM companies have consistently followed over the years — achieving scale first, and moving into higher-end markets later, Ma said. CXMT's technology iteration has accelerated in recent months. The company's LPDDR6 products and fifth-generation DRAM platform, G5, are both in mass production, suggesting a faster commercialization cycle. "It implies progress in new chip manufacturing, packaging, testing and reliability engineering," Tian said. Ma said that CXMT's latest move is likely to add real pressure to other DRAM memory makers, as Chinese suppliers increasingly target higher-end applications. For China's semiconductor sector, it offers a new anchor point to stride into high-performance memory and reduce dependence on overseas technology. Competition is intensifying amid a booming DRAM market. In the second quarter of 2026, Samsung Electronics led the global DRAM market with a 39 percent share, followed by SK Hynix's 26 percent and Micron Technology's 25 percent, an industry report showed on August 4, 2026. CXMT's global market share has reached 10 percent now, according to Counterpoint Research.

item.title: China's Ministry of National Defense slams Lai's 'Double Ten' speech for hyping up 'mainland military threat,' pursuing 'Taiwan independence'
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11 12:14:00
China's Ministry of National Defense China's Ministry of National Defense spokesperson on Sunday slammed Taiwan regional leader Lai Ching-te's so-called "Double Ten" speech for hyping up "mainland military threat" and pushing increased defense spending, saying Lai's remarks expose his attempt to seek "Taiwan independence" through military buildup and by soliciting external support. According to reports, Lai Ching-te recently delivered his so-called "Double Ten" speech, in which he hyped up claims that the Chinese mainland has continued to use military actions to pressure the Taiwan region and change the status quo across the Taiwan Straits, while calling for increased defense spending and stronger "whole-of-society defense resilience." In response, spokesperson Chen Xi said that there is only one China in the world, and Taiwan is part of China. This is the true status quo across the Taiwan Straits. Lai stubbornly clings to a "Taiwan independence" position, distorts right and wrong, hypes up the so-called "mainland military threat," and incites confrontation across the Straits. His attempts to seek "Taiwan independence" through military buildup and by soliciting external support.once again expose his nature as a source of trouble for Taiwan and a threat to peace, Chen said. In recent years, for their own partisan interests, the DPP authorities have pursued "independence" and resisted reunification, courted external forces, pushed so-called "whole-of-society mobilization" and attempted to turn the entire island into a battlefield. In doing so, they are tying the residents of Taiwan to the chariot of "Taiwan independence," undermining stability across the Taiwan Straits and sacrificing the Taiwan region's future, Chen said. The spokesperson noted that the PLA's regular exercises and training around the Taiwan island are aimed at deterring separatist moves for "Taiwan independence" and interference by external forces, and at safeguarding the security and well-being of residents in Taiwan. They are fully justified and beyond reproach. Chen said that "Taiwan independence" is fundamentally incompatible with peace across the Taiwan Straits. National reunification is an irresistible historical trend, a just cause and the aspiration of the people. We hope that Taiwan compatriots will fully recognize the extreme danger and harm posed by the Lai authorities' obstinate pursuit of "Taiwan independence," and join us in resolutely opposing "Taiwan independence" separatist forces and external interference, jointly safeguarding a peaceful and tranquil homeland and sharing the benefits and glory of national rejuvenation, Chen said. Global Times

item.title: Total ethane production at Northwest China's Tarim Oilfield exceeds 4 million tons: media report
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11 12:09:00
The Kela 2-5 well in Tarim Oilfield's Kela 2 gas field in Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Photo: screenshot of CMG's report Cumulative ethane production at the Tarim Oilfield in Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region has exceeded 4 million tons, reaching 4.08 million tons as of Saturday. This marks a new milestone in the deep processing of natural gas in the Tarim Basin, China Central Television (CCTV) reported, citing China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC), the oilfield's operator. Ethane is an important component of natural gas and a core feedstock for ethylene production. Further processing of ethylene yields plastics, chemical fibers, and various types of other industrial materials, making ethane a fundamental raw material for modern petrochemical industry. The Tarim Energy Company, located in Xinjiang's Luntai County, has an annual natural gas processing capacity of 25 billion cubic meters. The company's Lunnan natural gas deep-processing project is one of the largest single-unit natural gas deep-processing facilities at an oil and gas field in China, according to the CCTV report. The Tarim Energy Company operates under CNPC's Tarim Oilfield. Since its commissioning, it has processed a total of 56 billion cubic meters of natural gas, and produced 4.08 million tons of ethane and 2.8 million tons of light hydrocarbons and liquefied petroleum gas. The project has also achieved independent and controllable production, with core equipment such as propane refrigeration machines, compressors, and high-speed regeneration gas compressors having all replaced by domestically produced alternatives, an engineer at the Tarim Energy Company, was quoted as saying in the CCTV report. In recent years, Tarim Oilfield has advanced the "West-to-West" gas utilization strategy, promoting large-scale processing of natural gas resources and extending the downstream chemical industry chain. To date, the oilfield has built a pipeline network of more than 5,400 kilometers around the Tarim Basin, supplying over 7 billion cubic meters of gas annually to southern Xinjiang. Natural gas in the Tarim Basin is rich in ethane. The deep extraction of the heavier components from pipeline gas not only significantly increases the value of the natural gas resources but also provides China's ethylene industry with an independent, controllable and low-cost source of feedstock, the report said. Global Times

item.title: No Chinese casualties reported in Riyadh airport attack that kills 12, injures over 300: embassy
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11 09:19:00
This photo taken with a mobile phone on Sept. 19, 2026 shows thick smoke rising near King Khalid International Airport in northeastern Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Photo: Xinhua The Chinese Embassy in Saudi Arabia said on Sunday morning that no Chinese nationals had been reported killed or injured so far, following an attack on King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday afternoon. Twelve people have been killed and 309 others injured in the attack, the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation said. According to its statement posted early Sunday on social media platform X, the authority said the fatalities included four Saudi citizens and eight foreign residents -two Bangladeshis and one each from the US, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan. The injured are receiving necessary medial care at several hospitals, with some in serious condition, the authority said, adding that material damage was still being assessed. The Chinese Embassy and Consulates on Sunday urged Chinese-funded institutions and Chinese nationals in Saudi Arabia to remain firmly aware of potential risks, minimize non-essential outdoor activities, remain calm, and ensure their personal safety. Passengers planning to travel by air are advised to stay in close contact with their respective airlines to avoid disruptions to their travel plans, the embassy said in its statement on WeChat account. Chinese nationals planning to transit through Saudi Arabia are also advised to carefully reconsider their travel plans in view of the current aviation situation in the country. Foreign embassies in Riyadh, including those of the US, the United Kingdom, Ireland and Canada, issued advisories on social media to their citizens in Saudi Arabia, according to an Al Jazeera report. Earlier on Saturday, King Khalid airport urged passengers to contact their airlines directly and check their flight status before heading to the airport amid reports of disruptions to air traffic. The airport did not specify the cause of the disruptions in its initial advisory, the report noted. Following reports of the latest attack, US President Donald Trump was asked by reporters outside the White House whether Washington planned to join the Saudi strikes on the Houthis. "We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision. We move very quickly," he said, per the media report. Yemen's Houthi group has repeatedly targeted the airport in recent days. The latest attacks came amid an escalation in Yemen, where the Saudi-backed government forces are fighting the Houthis, the Xinhua News Agency reported. Global Times

item.title: Xinjiang scientific expedition finds "most resilient desert plant"
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11 07:33:00
Li Xiaoshuang (L), a researcher at Xinjiang Institute of Ecology and Geography under the Chinese Academy of Sciences, discusses Syntrichia caninervis' extraordinary resilience under extreme environments with her student in Urumqi, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, July 5, 2024. (Xinjiang Institute of Ecology and Geography under the Chinese Academy of Sciences/Handout via Xinhua) A type of moss discovered in a desert in northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region can survive conditions that would kill most plants, including severe dehydration, intense radiation, extreme cold and Mars-like space environments. This finding is among the major advances of the Third Xinjiang Scientific Expedition, which were released on Saturday in Urumqi, the regional capital city. Scientists describe the moss, Syntrichia caninervis, as "the most resilient desert plant found to date." The latest evidence of its remarkable resilience was uncovered in space. In March this year, the dried moss was carried aboard China's test cargo spacecraft Qingzhou for an orbital life-restart experiment. Facing microgravity and cosmic radiation, a controlled watering system gave the plants only a tiny amount of liquid water. Yet, the dried moss revived, changing from gray-black to yellow-green. "This is the first case in which a complete plant has been brought into low Earth orbit and successfully revived," said Li Xiaoshuang, a researcher at the Xinjiang Institute of Ecology and Geography under the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Continued in-orbit observation found the moss regenerating and thriving, indicating that it is an ideal material for deep-space life science research, Li added. In 2024, Li, as the first author, published the moss study in an academic journal, The Innovation, saying it is a promising pioneer plant for "colonizing extraterrestrial environments." This simulated image shows China's next-generation cargo craft Qingzhou docking with China's space station in orbit. (Innovation Academy for Microsatellites of the Chinese Academy of Sciences/Handout via Xinhua) Before the space test, scientists had already determined its genetic potential on Earth. Researchers of the Xinjiang scientific expedition discovered the plant in the Gurbantunggut Desert. After lab analysis, researchers found that the plant could tolerate the dehydration of more than 98 percent of its cells, survive rapid freezing at minus 196 degrees Celsius, and overcome strong gamma radiation. To understand how it endures such extremes, researchers obtained high-quality chromosome-level genetic information and found a large number of stress-related genes, unraveling the molecular code underlying this species' tolerance to extreme conditions. It can provide genetic material for improving crops and restoring desertified land, Li said. The Third Xinjiang Scientific Expedition was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Science and Technology. The previous two were conducted in the 1950s and 1980s, respectively. Over the past five years, the expedition team carried out studies on Xinjiang's ecology, land and agriculture, biodiversity and biological resources, mineral, energy and water resources.

item.title: Lai's speech rife with deception, covertness, misleadingness and danger: Hai Feng
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10 22:04:00
Illustration: Xia Qing/GT Lai Ching-te's so-called "Double Ten" speech this year dressed up an illusory picture in so-called people-centered livelihood, universal values and a vision of peace - in a "city upon a hill," children enjoy allowances, young people live and work in contentment, the elderly receive care, and industries steadily improve. He kept peddling the rhetoric of democracy, freedom and peace, claiming that increasing defense investment is meant to "deter war." If one merely listened to these words, it would be easy to mistake this for a heartwarming governing report. Yet what makes it most alarming is precisely that it sounds too good. The deceptive, covert, misleading and dangerous nature of the speech is concentrated in two elements: a so-called "city upon a hill" built on "blank checks," and a false narrative portraying the mainland as a "threat to peace." Running through the whole speech is an underlying thread: exploiting livelihood visions to rake in electoral support, employing value-laden rhetoric familiar to the West to court external sympathy, and shifting the blame for cross-Straits tensions onto the mainland. Deceptiveness: Dressing up unfulfilled promises as happiness within easy reach Lai spent a large portion of his speech showcasing so-called "economic achievements," citing growth rates, per-capita GDP and stock market index, before announcing a series of proposed welfare measures, ranging from child allowances and social housing for newlyweds and families, to long-term care and pension security. The picture it paints looks nice: the economy is growing, the government is flush with money, so people's lives will naturally get better and better. But ordinary people do not live by macro figures. How exactly is the NT$5,000-a-month growth allowance to be delivered, and how will its funding be secured? Behind the economic data, who is accountable for livelihood issues like "toxic oil," and how will they be resolved? Clearly, Lai is passing off "promises" as "achievements" and writing problems yet to be solved as answers about to be delivered. And the very implementation details that most need to be accounted for are deliberately concealed behind the "big pie" of the so-called "city upon a hill." Han Kuo-yu, in his speech the same day, voiced concern that Taiwan region is trapped in the predicament of "high-tech industries laughing all the way while traditional industries suffer." That remark laid bare the "Dutch disease" crisis now confronting Taiwan region's economy: growth that relies excessively on a single industry cannot replace the shared gains of industries across the board. At the end of the speech, Lai once again brought up the upcoming "nine-in-one" local elections. Welfare promises, appeals for unity and election mobilization appeared side by side in the same speech - which lends the "city upon a hill" another layer of meaning: it may well be nothing more than a "big pie" dangled to win votes. Covertness: Concealing "Taiwan independence" separatist attempts behind lies of livelihood and peace On the surface, from start to finish, Lai did not shout any fiery confrontational slogans. In reality, however, he spoke first of children, the elderly and housing, and then of so-called "national security"; first of protecting people's lives, and then of "strengthening defense" and "uniting democratic forces." This is how he wove livelihood and defense together layer by layer, ultimately steering toward his "Taiwan independence" separatist agenda. The covert nature of this rhetoric lies in the fact that each layer is appealing when heard on its own. Who would oppose caring for children? Who does not want social security? Who would not wish for peace? Yet none of these amounts to the "Taiwan independence" line. In his speech, Lai framed cross-Straits relations in a "state-to-state" posture and reduced complex historical and practical issues to the claim that "the future of Taiwan will be decided by the people of Taiwan." While professing his willingness to engage in exchanges, he laid down the distorted premise that Taiwan would "not accept subordination"; while pledging to cherish peace, he smeared all of the mainland's legitimate actions as "authoritarian pressure." He used peace and exchanges merely as decorative opening remarks - in essence, this is nothing more than the repackaged "Taiwan independence" fallacy. Misleadingness: Distorting the Taiwan question through Western narrative Lai's speech was clearly also performed for external forces. Using the Western narrative framework of "democracy versus authoritarianism" and "freedom versus aggression," he unilaterally portrayed Taiwan region as a "defender of democracy" and a "victim of authoritarianism," distorted the mainland into the side undermining peace, and sought to elicit "sympathy" from the international community. This is deliberately meant to muddle the historical context and legal facts of the Taiwan question, to conceal the fact that the real culprit behind the evolution of the cross-Straits situation is "Taiwan independence," and to blur the negative impact that the collusion between "Taiwan independence" separatist forces and external interventionist forces has brought to the world. "Taiwan independence" and cross-Straits peace and stability are fundamentally irreconcilable. Lai magnified the mainland's military operations and so-called "gray-zone activities," falsely claiming that the mainland intends to change the status quo. He cherry-picked fragments of information while omitting the "Taiwan independence" advocacy, external intervention, and the chain of reactions they have triggered. He tried to present the international community with a cropped picture - as if the tension across the Straits stems from the mainland, and as if the Taiwan regional authorities are merely engaged in "passive defense." Compared with blunt political slogans, this rhetoric is more deceptive, easier to enter the Western public-opinion arena, and easier to package the Taiwan question as a "battle of values" in which the international community must take sides. The more deceptive it is, the more it warrants vigilance. Danger: Staking security on external backing while leaving the risks to the people of Taiwan Lai claims that increasing defense investment is meant to "deter war" and that strengthening self-defense does not mean abandoning dialogue. This is a complete lie. If the Taiwan regional authorities continue to organize their political narrative around alleged mainland's "threat of aggression" and continue to stake their security on external powers such as the US and Japan, the space for cross-Straits dialogue will only narrow further. And once a conflict erupts in the Taiwan Straits, it is the people of Taiwan who would bear the brunt - external forces would only weigh whether to intervene according to their own interests. The "confidence" Lai shows is, to a large extent, likely emboldened by some external forces. But external backing has never been an unlimited guarantee. When the assumption that "someone will protect Taiwan" is treated as a justification for ceaselessly probing the limits of risk, the more that confidence swells, the greater the uncertainty the people of Taiwan will face. Lai repeatedly extolled democracy and freedom, yet at the same occasion Han pointed out that democracy within the island has cracked and voiced the sharp criticism of "fake democracy, real dictatorship." Lai invoked "democracy" merely to adorn his facade and sing its praises. But since taking office, the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities have brazenly launched the "mass recall" campaign, used judicial means to hunt down opposition forces, and wielded the refusal to countersign documents to resist checks and balances. These repeated misdeeds have spawned a "green terror" within the island, torn Taiwan's society apart step by step, and long since run counter to democracy. Han put forward three wishes - Taiwan's security, people with money, and long live democracy - which can be used to test Lai's "city upon a hill" narrative: Can security be built on easing cross-Straits confrontation? Can economic dividends reach the pockets of ordinary people? Can democracy accommodate differing political views? These are questions that a pretentious speech cannot answer. Lai may use rhetoric to conjure up a "city upon a hill," but cross-Straits peace cannot be achieved through lies and deception. Winning votes with promises that cannot be honored, courting sympathy with narratives that pander to the West, shirking responsibility and shifting contradictions with distorted rhetoric, and finally leveraging external backing to feed his "independence" ambitions - this is precisely what makes Lai 's speech most worthy of vigilance. The people of Taiwan need to see clearly: the prettier the words, the more one must ask who will actually deliver on them; the deeper the "Taiwan independence" slogans are buried, the more one must ask who will be footing the bill for the enormous risks.

item.title: China aims to return Mars samples around 2031, scientist says
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10 13:07:00
China’s Tianwen-3 mission is scheduled to launch around 2028 Schematic diagram: VCG China aims to return samples from Mars to Earth in around 2031, with the Tianwen-3 mission scheduled to launch around 2028, Zhang Jiajun, an associate research fellow at the Shanghai Astronomical Observatory of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, wrote in an article titled "Why do we venture to Mars?" published by the People's Daily on Saturday. Zhang noted that three major challenges must be addressed before humans can establish a presence on Mars: the exchange of information between Earth and Mars, the transport of materials between the two planets, and human survival on the Red Planet. For communication and spacecraft navigation, the very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) orbit determination system led by the Shanghai Astronomical Observatory can precisely measure the trajectories of spacecraft traveling to Mars, helping ensure successful orbital insertion. The technology has been preliminarily validated during China's Tianwen-1 Mars mission, Zhang wrote. The second challenge is the exchange of physical materials between Earth and Mars. While humans can send spacecraft to the planet, they have yet to develop the capability to collect Martian material and return it to Earth, Zhang noted. On May 15, 2021, a lander carrying China's first Mars rover touched down on Mars, marking the first time China has landed a probe on a planet other than Earth, Xinhua reported. China plans to return samples from Mars to Earth around 2031, with the Tianwen-3 mission scheduled to launch around 2028, Zhang said. The third challenge is ensuring human survival. Mars has extremely low temperatures, high radiation levels, low gravity, low atmospheric pressure, and limited access to water and oxygen. How to use the planet's local resources to support human activities remains an area requiring further exploration, Zhang wrote. Despite these challenges, Mars remains an attainable target as humanity ventures beyond the Earth-moon system into deep space, Zhang said. Mercury is too close to the Sun, Venus has a hostile environment, and other celestial bodies are much farther away. By comparison, Mars offers more favorable conditions, including a thin atmosphere, water ice, and a rotation period and seasonal cycles similar to Earth's. These characteristics make it a suitable stepping stone for humanity's journey toward an interplanetary civilization, he wrote. "My work focuses on cosmology, and my colleagues and I are working toward a dream that can be realized, taking one step at a time to make a round trip to Mars a reality," Zhang said. Global Times

item.title: Multiple Chinese regions announce spring, autumn holidays for primary, secondary school students, boosting parent-child travel: media
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10 11:12:00
Students wait with their parents to board a train for an autumn holiday trip in Jinhua, East China’s Zhejiang Province on November 12, 2025. Photo: VCG Several regions, in provinces including South China's Guangdong Province, Southwest China's Sichuan Province, and North China's Shanxi Province, have announced autumn holiday schedules for second and primary school students. The breaks generally last three to four days, with some arranged alongside weekends to form five-day holidays, CCTV News reported on Saturday. Shenzhen in Guangdong Province has scheduled a four-day autumn break from November 17 to 20 for schools in compulsory education phase. Zigong and Panzhihua in Sichuan Province will have autumn holidays from November 16 to 18 and November 18 to 20, respectively, while Yuncheng in Shanxi Province has scheduled its break for November 5, 6 and 9. Cities across Hunan Province have also announced arrangements, with most breaks concentrated in mid-November. Some regions have also announced spring holiday dates for 2027, with no make-up working days scheduled after the spring and autumn breaks, according to CCTV News. In recent years, as the "double reduction" policy aimed at easing students' academic burdens has been implemented, calls for more flexible school schedules have grown louder, Xinhua reported. Although winter and summer vacations are longer, they often coincide with peak travel seasons. Spring and autumn breaks can help families avoid crowds and give parents opportunities to travel with their children at a more relaxed pace, CCTV News reported. The introduction of spring and autumn holidays also reflects a shift in educational thinking, recognizing that learning takes place not only in classrooms but also in nature, rural settings and during travel, according to the report. However, the mismatch between children's school holidays and parents' work schedules remains a challenge, as students may be off school while their parents continue working. Experts suggest that implementing spring and autumn holidays requires coordination among families, schools and society. They also call for the effective implementation of paid leave policies and encourage staggered vacations to help parents take time off at different periods and ensure students can make meaningful use of their holidays, CCTV News reported. Global Times

item.title: The louder protectionism roars, the more precious China-EU dialogue becomes: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10 00:52:00
China EU Photo:VCG At a time when global challenges continue to emerge, the significance of China-EU relations has long extended beyond the bilateral sphere. By continuously deepening their economic ties and shared interests, China and the EU can not only unleash the innovative potential of their respective markets but also reinforce each other's development and contribute to global economic recovery. From Thursday to Friday, China and the EU held the second meeting of their bilateral trade and investment consultation mechanism in Beijing. The two sides engaged in pragmatic and productive discussions, reaching a 16-point consensus covering trade and investment balances, export controls, intellectual property rights and reform of the World Trade Organization (WTO). Against the backdrop of a sluggish global economic recovery and undercurrents of anti-globalization, this is a pragmatic step to properly handle bilateral differences and a crucial display of responsibility by China and the EU in injecting stability and certainty into the global economy amid turbulent times. A closer look at this list reveals its core value: anchored in rules-based governance and bridged by mutual trust, it demonstrates the political wisdom to manage differences and steer China-EU economic and trade relations toward greater stability and balance. The first item on the list states that both sides will continue to explore the possibility of reducing tariffs on certain products within the WTO framework. In the hybrid vehicle trade sector, which has attracted significant public attention, the two sides agreed to reach a mutual understanding in a manner consistent with WTO rules, providing a pathway to ease the previously deadlocked trade dispute. In the field of export controls, China expressed its willingness to continue facilitating export license approvals for rare earths and permanent magnets bound for the EU through a "green channel" mechanism. The two sides also included "advance notifications before items are added to control lists" in the consensus list. This arrangement improves the transparency in listing and delisting procedures, helping to reduce misjudgments and stabilize expectations. This list covers a significant portion of the current challenges and bottlenecks in economic and trade relations between China and the EU, and the consensus reached by both sides demonstrates that no matter how complex trade frictions may be, pragmatic solutions can always be found as long as both sides uphold the spirit of dialogue and adhere to equal-footed consultation. The convergence of interests is the inevitable outcome of economic globalization and more so a powerful engine driving common prosperity for China, the EU, and the world at large. In 2025, China-EU trade in goods exceeded $800 billion, with their combined economic output accounting for over one-third of the global total, bilateral trade volume making up nearly one-quarter of the world's total, and nearly half of bilateral trade consisting of intermediate goods. The long-standing pattern of "trade surpluses in China and profits in Europe" has made the two sides a community of shared interests, with each deeply intertwined with the other. This also demonstrates that as long as China and the EU work together, the synergies they generate will far outweigh the narrow calculations of a zero-sum game, creating vast new opportunities for industrial upgrading and improving the well-being of their peoples. Protectionism cannot enhance competitiveness, while decoupling and severing supply chains will only harm others without benefiting oneself. By continuously deepening their economic ties and shared interests, China and the EU can not only unleash the innovative potential of their respective markets but also reinforce each other's development and contribute to global economic recovery. As a major strategic force in the world, Europe should uphold its tradition of multilateralism and strategic autonomy, rather than allow itself to be swept up in the tide of protectionism and the excessive securitization of economic issues. At the moment, unilateralism is on the rise, with certain major powers frequently imposing sanctions in an attempt to weaponize economic and trade issues. Europe has a deep-rooted tradition of free trade and should not simply follow the crowd, much less turn security anxieties into trade barriers. As China has repeatedly and sincerely pointed out, the EU should remain committed to openness, cooperation and free trade, abide by WTO rules, not resort to protectionist tools at every turn, and, above all, refrain from politicizing and excessively securitizing economic and trade issues - so as to avoid pursuing misguided policies that will ultimately backfire on itself. China is not the root cause of the EU's problems, but a partner in addressing them. Faced with a complex external environment, Europe can only truly safeguard its fundamental interests amid changes unseen in a century by taking a long-term view of the economic and trade relations between China and the EU and adhering to equal-footed dialogue and consultation. Looking ahead to future arrangements for institutionalized consultations, China and the EU should overcome obstacles through sustained dialogue and work together to provide stability and certainty to the world. The two sides have agreed to hold the third regular meeting under the mechanism in March 2027 and maintain close communication in the meantime, including a ministerial-level video meeting in January 2027. Such institutionalized and regular arrangements provide an important safeguard for bridging differences and deepening cooperation. At a time when global challenges continue to emerge, the significance of China-EU relations has long extended beyond the bilateral sphere. In the face of an international landscape marked by intertwined turbulence and transformation, China and the EU should be partners that build mutual trust rather than systemic rivals, and promoters of cooperation rather than instigators of friction. We look forward to both China and the EU seizing this opportunity presented by the consultations to continue deepening cooperation based on equal dialogue and mutual benefit, translating more consensus into concrete actions, ensuring that the benefits of China-EU economic and trade cooperation continue to benefit the people of both sides, and injecting more warmth and confidence into a global economy fraught with uncertainty.

item.title: How China achieved its photovoltaic turnaround
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09 21:21:00
Solar rooftop photovoltaic power generation facilities are seen on a building in Qingdao, East China's Shandong Province, on June 23, 2026. Photo: VCG By the end of July, China's installed capacity of solar panels reached 1.286 billion kilowatts in China, surpassing that of coal power for the first time to become the nation's largest power source by installed capacity. In China, photovoltaic (PV) power has shifted from a "satellite-exclusive luxury" to a power source cheaper than coal. This remarkable turnaround offers deep insights into industrial growth and the fundamental laws of energy transition. The essence of this turnaround lies in locking the market and the factories into a single closed-loop system, driving that ecosystem toward systematic synergy and high-efficiency operation. To get this virtuous cycle spinning, the first step was a vigorous push to expand the domestic market. China has been leveraging policy coordination to anchor and open up the domestic market. Measures included shifting subsidies entirely to actual power generation output with 20-year guaranteed terms. This not only plugged loopholes prone to subsidy fraud but also provided stable, long-term revenue streams, turning solar farms into bankable assets that financial institutions were willing to lend to. The foresight of this policy lay not merely in daring to invest when solar costs remained high, but in building a mechanism that forced costs downward rather than simply throwing subsidies at enterprises to keep them afloat. Truly effective industrial policy does not replace the market; rather, it allows market forces to play out fully over long cycles. Once the market opened, cost reduction shifted to continuous technological innovation, driven by compounding, chain-reaction improvements rather than single breakthroughs. Innovations like diamond wire saws slashed silicon wafer costs and established mono-crystalline wafers as the mainstream choice, a trajectory mirrored by PERC solar cell technology. These technologies were not originally invented in China, but why were their industrialization fates ultimately rewritten in Chinese workshops? The reason lies in China's comprehensive, all-inclusive industrial supply chains and intense market competition. The moment a new manufacturing process is successfully verified and run at a single company, domestic equipment suppliers immediately step up with iterative upgrades, and industry peers race to expand production capacity, achieving widespread adoption across the entire sector within a few years. Today, China's PV industry R&D strength has entered the global vanguard. Besides, technology dictates the content of learning, while scale determines its speed. China accounts for over 80 percent of manufacturing output across all segments of the solar supply chain, meaning the vast majority of global PV industrial experience has been accumulated in China. The true weight of China's scaled industrial capacity lies in the fact that its expanding output can, by and large, find genuine, real-world demand to absorb it, be it at home or abroad. When supply can be manufactured and demand can absorb it, costs can slide steadily down the "learning curve." Of course, the industry faces pressing real-world challenges in integration and absorption. On the power grid side, midday surges in solar generation coupled with insufficient support during evening peak hours mean that energy storage deployment and market mechanisms urgently need strengthening. On the industrial side, harmonizing industrial policy with effective measures to curb cutthroat price competition and realigning the supply side with genuine market demand are vital tasks for the period ahead. From a "luxury item on satellites" to a ubiquitous fixture on deserts, rooftops, and fish ponds, solar power has journeyed for over seven decades since the invention of the silicon solar cell. The answer behind China's solar turnaround is hardly a secret: policy guided the market back home, an integrated supply chain system translated innovation into scaled manufacturing capacity, and an ultra-large market and application ecosystem further refined that capacity into seasoned industrial expertise. Chinese enterprises had paid the "tuition fee," and today, the dividends and hard-earned lessons of cost reduction are shared with the world. For the world, the profound significance of China's PV turnaround lies in shattering conventional mindsets: energy security does not have to be entirely tethered to underground reserves and maritime trade routes; at least a portion of it can be forged right inside a workshop.
